Subject: Staging safety sweep + rollback scenarios for private deployment — GlobeMed

Hi Samir / infra team,

Quick context: GlobeMed's private VPC deployment is scheduled for the minor platform patch we discussed. Before we push the pin to tenant fleets, I'd like to run a short, targeted safety sweep in your staging environment to validate our pinned-runtime + KV cache behaviour and exercise rollback paths.

Goals for the sweep:
- Validate pinned model variant loads correctly (same binary + quant profile).
- Confirm KV/prefix cache warmup and eviction boundaries under simulated traffic.
- Run rollback and confirm state-resume with minimal cold-start latency.
- Check observability: per-route token breakdowns, p95 latency, error spike detection.

Proposed window: Friday 2026-11-28 09:00–11:00 PT (canary + controlled ramp). If that doesn't work for you, propose an alternative.

Attached: initial_sanity_checklist.md — small checklist for staging ops.

Next steps I need from you:
1) Confirm you can run the canary+rollback script from staging.
2) Confirm the on-call list and an estimated lead time to roll back if we hit the abort criteria.
3) Any constraints on maintenance windows in your VPC (eg. backup snapshots that block restarts).

Thanks — I want to keep this short and actionable.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Looping in the technical checklist and the pin/rollback specifics we discussed in the onboarding workshop. High level: we will pin the 1.4.2-quant build and the KV-cache will be warmed via a prefix replay. Rollback is a two-step: 

1) Rollback marker: run rollout_abort.sh which flips routing to the previous 1.4.1-config variant and drains the new pods.
2) State rehydration: run cache-hydrate.sh against the previous variant to reduce cold starts.

Quick checklist items for ops (explicit):
- Ensure network ACLs allow internal health probes from 10.12.0.0/16.
- Pre-create a snapshot of the model store (s3-compatible) identified as glbmd-20261128-snap.
- Tag the canary hosts with maintenance:glbmd-20261128 and set traffic_shaper to 5% initially.
- Disable the aggressive prefix-eviction policy for the canary hosts.

Abort criteria (immediate rollback):
- 5xx error rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m
- p95 response latency increase > 50% relative to baseline
- Embeddings skew (cosine) > 2% on spot-check prompts

Rollback (graceful) acceptance: system must report < 0.2% 5xx and p95 within 20% of baseline for 30m.

Attachment: rollback-scripts-list.txt (text/plain, 3 KB) — contains the scripts: rollout_abort.sh, cache-hydrate.sh, verify-state.sh

Dev

Thanks — couple of operational guardrails and escalation notes from my side:

Canary success thresholds (proposed):
- 5xx < 0.5% over 5m (abort if breached)
- p95 latency delta vs baseline < 20 ms (abort if > 50 ms)
- Token cost regression < 3%
- Embedding accuracy drift < 1% on our regression set

Escalation flow if abort:
1) Ops toggles routing via rollout_abort.sh and pages on-call (Samir).
2) If state rehydration fails, page Platform Eng (Jonas then Dev) and open an incident bridge.
3) If we cannot reach pre-patch baseline within 30 minutes, we escalate to contract-level SLA and consider a reimage of canary hosts.

Also: please include a short smoke suite that hits these endpoints: /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings, /internal/kv-status. We need clear telemetry per-route.

Related link: https://redwood.app/drive/GlobeMed-upgrade-plan-v2

Jonas
Engineering Manager, Runtime
